title: X-Ray Astronomy: Hot Gas, X-Ray Binaries and the Diffuse X-Ray Background Against Density and Energy Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor James Reed, and this is X-Ray Astronomy: Hot Gas, X-Ray Binaries and the Diffuse X-Ray Background Against Density and Energy Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor James Reed, and this is X-Ray Astronomy: Hot Gas, X-Ray Binaries and the Diffuse X-Ray Background Against Density and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: coolcore electron density at 100 kpc = 0.0132 per cm^3; typical gas mass within 1 Mpc = 6.43e+13 solar masses; typical bolometric luminosity within 1 Mpc = 1.56e+45 erg/s; merger electron density at 500 kpc = 0.0012 per cm^3; typical central mass density as a fraction of the density bound = 2.01e-81.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Cluster Counts in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey: Integrating the Luminosity Function Over the Sky'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: comoving volume to redshift 0.5 over the extragalactic sky = 1.85e+10 Mpc^3; expected clusters above that luminosity within redshift 0.5 = 1.77e+05 clusters; expected clusters above that luminosity within redshift 0.5 = 1.57e+04 clusters; luminosity corresponding to flux 1e-13 at redshift 0.3 = 2.88e+43 erg/s; luminosity corresponding to flux 1e-13 at redshift 0.5 = 9.60e+43
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Cooling Times in Cluster Cores: Where Radiative Losses Outrun the Age of the Universe'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: cooling time at n=0.05 per cm^3 and 4 keV = 9.37e+08 years; cooling time at n=0.01 per cm^3 and 6 keV = 6.16e+09 years; cooling radius where the cooling time equals 7.7 Gyr = 150 kpc; classical mass deposition rate inside the cooling radius = 577 solar masses per year; cooling time of the typical core as a fraction of the Hubble time = 0.447.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Deep-Field Source Counts: The Log N-Log S Relation and the Resolved Fraction of the Background'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: cumulative source count above flux 1e-15 erg/cm^2/s = 1.7e+03 per deg^2; cumulative source count above flux 1e-16 erg/cm^2/s = 1.20e+04 per deg^2; fraction of the background resolved by the counts integral = 0.814; whole-sky source count above 1e-15 erg/cm^2/s = 7.01e+07 sources; flux above which half of the resolved intensity originates = 1.18e-14 erg/cm^2/s.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Eddington Luminosities and Ultraluminous X-Ray Sources: The Mass, Beaming and Super-Eddington Budgets'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: Eddington luminosity of a 1.4 solar mass accretor = 1.76e+38 erg/s; Eddington luminosity of a 10 solar mass accretor = 1.26e+39 erg/s; minimum mass radiating 1e40 erg/s at the Eddington limit = 79.5 solar masses; beaming factor required for a 10 solar mass black hole to appear at 1e40 erg/s = 0.126; Eddington ratio of a 30 solar mass black hole radiating 1e40 erg/s = 2.65; E
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Galaxy Groups and the Steepened Luminosity-Temperature Relation: The Energy Cost of Raising Gas Entropy'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: luminosity deficit factor of groups at 1.0 keV = 5.52; luminosity deficit factor of groups at 0.5 keV = 8.97; energy to inject 1 keV per particle into the group gas = 1.59e+60 erg; injection energy as a fraction of binding energy = 0.00371; black hole mass whose accretion at ten per cent efficiency supplies the injection = 8.88e+06 solar masses; radiative cooling time of the
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound”. Its stated result is: The paper's headline computed results are: coolcore electron density at 100 kpc = 0.0132 per cm^3; typical gas mass within 1 Mpc = 6.43e+13 solar masses; typical bolometric luminosity within 1 Mpc = 1.56e+45 erg/s; merger electron density at 500 kpc = 0.0012 per cm^3; typical central mass density as (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound'; 'Cluster Counts in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey: Integrating the Luminosity Function Over the Sky'; 'Cooling Times in Cluster Cores: Where Radiative Losses Outrun the Age of the Universe'; 'Deep-Field Source Counts: The Log N-Log S Relation and the Resolved Fraction of the Background'; 'Eddington Luminosities and Ultraluminous X-Ray Sources: The Mass, Beaming and Super-Eddington Budgets'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound'. The result it reported gives a value for density at 100 kpc, and that value is what this question asks for.
questions.teach2: Here is the exact passage from the lesson again: 'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound'. Its stated result: The paper's headline computed results are: coolcore electron density at 100 kpc = 0.0132 per cm^3; typical gas mass within 1 Mpc = 6.43e+13 solar masses; typical bolometric luminosity within 1 Mpc = 1.56e+45 erg/s; merger electron density at 500 kpc = 0.0012 per cm^3; typical central mass density as a fraction of the density bound = 2.01e-81. And here is that same result with the words stripped away — just the quantities standing in a row: density at 100 kpc = 0.0132; mass within 1 Mpc = 6.43e+13; luminosity within 1 Mpc = 1.56e+45. Find density at 100 kpc in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: density at 100 kpc = 0.0132; mass within 1 Mpc = 6.43e+13; luminosity within 1 Mpc = 1.56e+45. (3) This question asks for the value paired with density at 100 kpc. (4) In that row, density at 100 kpc stands beside 0.0132 — so the answer the lesson gives is 0.0132. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Beta-Model Density Profiles of Cluster Gas: Gas Mass, Central Density and the Distance to Any Density Bound' reported a number for density at 100 kpc. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
